Resolve ... Names Against Canonical Parameter Names

Source: R/RcppExports.R
resolve_param_case.Rd

Matches the names of a captured ... list against a set of canonical parameter names, ignoring case, and writes the matched values into the calling frame. Matched elements are dropped from the returned list, so the caller can forward what is left as genuine ....

Usage

resolve_param_case(dots, canonical, env, lower_inner = FALSE)

Arguments

dots

A list, typically list(...) from the calling function. Its names are compared against canonical.

canonical

A character vector of canonical parameter names, typically rlang::fn_fmls_names(). The exact spelling of a matched entry is used as the name of the variable assigned in env.

env

An environment, typically rlang::current_env(), in which the canonical parameters live. Matched parameters are written here; they are not part of the returned list.

lower_inner

A logical flag. When TRUE, the inner names of every matched list are lowercased as well, so list(Alpha = list(MaxIter = 1)) becomes list(Alpha = list(maxiter = 1)).

Value

A named list holding the elements of dots that were not matched, in their original order. Its length may be zero.

Details

This is a helper for functions that accept a fixed set of named sub-argument lists (for example bench_config) but want to tolerate BenchRounds as well as bench_rounds.

  • Matching is case-insensitive on the ASCII range only, and is otherwise exact: foo_bar does not match foo-bar. If canonical contains several names that differ only in case, the first one wins.

  • Each matched value must be a plain list, otherwise an error is raised naming the offending argument.

  • The current value of the canonical parameter is read from env (which forces its promise) and merged with the supplied value as modify_list(supplied, current): fields present in both take the value from env, fields only in the supplied list are added, nested lists are merged recursively, and NULL values are kept. The result is then assigned back to the canonical name in env.

  • When several supplied names match the same canonical parameter, they are processed in order, so the last one wins.

  • Elements of dots that are unnamed, or whose name is NA or "", are never matched and are returned unchanged.

  • If dots has no names at all, it is returned as is without any work.

  • Unmatched elements and untouched values are shared with the input, not copied.

See also

modify_list()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
f <- function(alpha = list(), ...) {
  dots <- resolve_param_case(
    dots = list(...),
    canonical = rlang::fn_fmls_names(),
    env = rlang::current_env(),
    lower_inner = TRUE
  )
  list(alpha = alpha, dots = dots)
}

# `Alpha` matches `alpha`; inner names are lowercased, `extra` is left over
f(Alpha = list(MaxIter = 10), extra = 1) |> str()

# non-list values are rejected
try(f(Alpha = 10))
} # }
